stemMd: Which statement correctly compares a chlorine atom and a chloride ion formed from it?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The chloride ion has no nucleus.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The two particles must have opposite nuclear charges.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They have the same proton count, but the chloride ion has one more electron.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The chlorine atom must have one fewer neutron.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The chloride ion has one more proton.

explanationMd: Chloride forms when chlorine gains an electron. The added negative charge produces Cl⁻ without changing the nucleus. Proton number determines the element, while electron number determines the ion’s charge relative to the neutral atom.

distractorRationale.d: Electron gain does not require a neutron change.
distractorRationale.a: Ion formation leaves the nucleus intact.
distractorRationale.b: Their nuclei have the same positive charge.
